messages:
Maya R: Heads up — az-west1 went into partial network quarantine ~08:12, control plane marked ~20% of nodes NotReady and the scheduler churned GPU pods.
Jon P: saw the alert, we're getting a bunch of tiny GPU pods pending and some mid-priority training jobs evicted. can we pause automated backfills?
Maya R: opsbot already started a mitigation hook to stop aggressive backfills. opsbot: mitigation applied — backfill=paused, warm-pool-scale=hold :white_check_mark:
Kumar: quick summary numbers: ~120 GPU pods in az-west1, 37 evicted in last 6m, fragmentation jumped from 18% -> 52% (estimated by slot-util histogram)
Sara L: cost note — if we reschedule those evicted jobs to us-east it will spike cross-region egress on dataset pulls. need to be mindful.
Jon P: agree. proposal: 1) quarantine remaining NotReady nodes, 2) run targeted defrag (preferentially co-locate tiny pods on warm-pool nodes), 3) throttle drains so we avoid cascade evictions.
Maya R: sounds right. can we do targeted taint+drain for just the flaky NIC nodes? example command:

```
kubectl taint nodes node-azw1-abc example/quarantine=true:NoSchedule
kubectl drain node-azw1-abc --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='app!=warm-pool'
```

Kumar: I'll generate a list of the top 10 nodes with highest retransmits and taint them. running script now.
Lin: should we enable preferAvoid for the scheduler or adjust topologySpread? we're getting lots of tiny single-gpu pods scattering across hosts.
Jon P: preferAvoid won't help immediate pressure. short term: enable pack-small-pods policy in the scheduler config (packThreshold=0.25) and bump warm-pool size by 4 GPUs. medium term: run offline compaction job to consolidate ephemeral pods.
Sara L: +1 but also set a rate limit on cross-region reschedules to protect egress budget. put a manual approval if estimated egress > 200GB.
opsbot: compaction-job queued on batch-runner-3, warm-pool requested +4 gpus in az-west1, approval lock set for egress >200GB.
Maya R: timeline? Kumar — how long to taint+drain the 10 nodes safely?
Kumar: ~12-15m for taint + cordon + graceful drain per node but we can parallelize 3 at a time -> finishing ~40m. I'll coordinate with Jon to limit concurrent drains.
Jon P: I'll reduce controller reclaim rate and pause autoscaler triggers while drains are ongoing.
Lin: once stable, let's run a quick evict-fairness check and make sure low-priority long jobs don't keep getting bounced. add a rule: prefer non-preemptible lane for the heavy training ones.
Maya R: good. after drains complete we should unblock backfills slowly with a 5m ramp and monitor eviction rate. post back to this thread when taints are applied.
Kumar: taints applied to first 3 nodes now, draining. posting pod counts in 5.
opsbot: automated monitor: eviction-rate (az-west1) -> 12/min -> target <2/min. alert if >5/min for 10m.
Maya R: thanks team. I'll follow up with a short postmortem draft once we confirm root cause (likely NIC flapping + failover path misconfig).
